summary.text: Second Steep replaced Kettlewick Tea Co.'s monthly win-back discount with a three-step Klaviyo flow built on each customer's own order history. In 26 weeks it brought back 781 lapsed customers, 9% of those who entered, and grew win-back revenue 2.7 times while the rest of the site grew 3%.

sections.text:
Kettlewick Tea Co. sells loose-leaf tea online to customers who reorder when a tin runs out. Until March 2026, every customer who went 120 days without an order received one monthly win-back email: the same discount, sent to the whole lapsed list. In the 26 weeks from September 1, 2025 to March 1, 2026, the six sends went out 49,800 times and produced $15,980 in revenue in GA4 on a last-click basis, or $0.34 per email in Klaviyo's count. The same customers saw the same offer month after month, and nothing in the email reflected what they used to buy.

On February 16, 2026, before launch, the team set two objectives for the replacement program, Second Steep: double win-back revenue against those 26 weeks, and bring back at least 5% of the lapsed customers who enter the program.

A survey of lapsed customers in February 2026 (412 responses) gave the insight: 46% said they had run out and forgotten to reorder, and 29% said they wanted to try something new. Neither group needed a discount first. One needed a reminder at the right moment; the other needed a reason to come back to a different tea.

So Second Steep replaced one blanket offer with a sequence that asks for less before it gives more. It opens with the customer's own last tea and a refill, moves to a tasting set picked from the flavours they ordered before, and keeps the discount for the end, only for customers who still haven't ordered. Every customer follows the same three steps, but what they see comes from their own order history, so a lapsed green-tea buyer is shown green teas, not the store's bestsellers.

Second Steep went live in Klaviyo on March 2, 2026 as a three-email flow, triggered when a customer passes 120 days without an order. On day 0, a reminder shows their last tea, with a one-click refill in the size they bought. On day 7, a tasting set offers three teas chosen from the flavour profile of their past orders. On day 21, a 15% code arrives that expires after seven days.

A customer who orders leaves the flow at once, so nobody who has come back receives the next email or the discount. Customers who open none of the three are paused from win-back email for 90 days to protect deliverability.

The monthly win-back send was switched off the same week, so the two never overlapped. The flow ran unchanged for the full 26 weeks entered here; the team changed only subject lines, through two A/B tests in April.

Both objectives were met. All figures cover the 26 weeks from March 2, 2026 to August 30, 2026, against the 26 weeks before (September 1, 2025 to March 1, 2026) and the same 26 weeks a year earlier (March 3, 2025 to August 31, 2025).

Objective 1, double win-back revenue: met. Win-back revenue in GA4, counted on a last-click basis, rose from $15,980 to $43,215, 2.7 times the 26 weeks before. Klaviyo's own attribution shows the same 2.7 times, from $17,240 to $46,891; we quote the lower GA4 figures. Against the same weeks a year earlier ($14,630), win-back revenue was 2.9 times higher, so the rise is not a seasonal effect.

Objective 2, bring back at least 5% of lapsed customers who enter: met. 7,960 lapsed customers entered Second Steep, and 781 of them ordered again: 9%, against the objective of 5%.

The store's own growth does not explain the rise. Revenue from the rest of the site, everything except win-back, grew 3% over the same windows, while win-back revenue grew 170%, a gap of 167 percentage points. Store orders overall rose 7% on the 26 weeks before.

Each email now earns more. Revenue per win-back email, in Klaviyo's count, rose from $0.34 to $2.23, and the program sent 20,990 emails against 49,800 for the old monthly send: 57% fewer emails for 2.7 times the revenue.

Klaviyo credits 336 returning customers to the day-0 reminder, 248 to the tasting set and 197 to the discount email, so 74% of the customers who came back did so before any discount was offered.
